lines: Want to shut down perimeter shooters?
This is how the three-two zone works.
Control the wings... and make outside shots difficult.
Ball to the wing: the nearest defender closes out...
and everyone shifts to protect the gaps.
The others rotate to protect the paint and cover the weak side.
If the ball gets inside, the middle defender must react,
and the whole defense has to adjust.
The three-two is great at contesting perimeter shots.
But the corners, the high post and defensive rebounding can become problems.
